requirements.requirement: On node1, serve a package repository from local storage.
requirements.summary: Direct observations show an enabled, active localrepo service serving repository metadata over HTTP with status 200. The repository contains the tree RPM and metadata, and yum resolves tree through local-storage. The service and identical payload checksums remained available after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while the remote repository is unreachable.
requirements.summary: The captured installation began with tree absent, observed the enabled remote endpoint timing out, and installed tree-1.6.0-10.el7 from local-storage. The binary ran successfully, and subsequent yum output attributed the installed package to @local-storage.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Node1 served a functional local RPM repository, installed and ran tree from that repository while the configured remote endpoint timed out, and retained the complete working state across the mandatory node restart.
limitations: The unreachable remote repository was an executor-configured TEST-NET endpoint; the baseline had no enabled yum repositories. Thus the evidence directly proves operation alongside an unreachable configured remote, but not failure of a pre-existing production repository.
The lifecycle package-health probe timed out both before and after execution, so global package consistency could not be independently compared.
The final lifecycle inventory covers /tmp but not /var/tmp, leaving the final presence of bootstrap downloads and benchmark-reboot.log unconfirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated or destructive mutation is evident: package downloads, signing-key import, repository tooling installation, repository configuration, service enablement, package installation, and reboot all had clear task or verification roles. The restart protocol was strong: a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, brief SSH disruption, and recovered service, repository data, package, and remote-unreachable condition were directly captured and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities. Minor hygiene residue remained in /tmp: remote-only.out, repomd-before.xml, and repomd-after.xml were evidence artifacts that were not cleaned up. The bootstrap directory and reboot log created under /var/tmp also had no explicit cleanup, although their final presence was not inventoried. No failed services were observed after execution.
